candidateAudit.title: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive na
candidateAudit.text: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive narrative obscures a deeper, more ‘errant’ truth? Media theorist and author Clemens Apprich in conversation with philosopher Jan Völker. Moderated by Amanda Holmes, Department of Philosophy, University of Applied Arts Vienna Welcome: Ulrike Kuch, Rector of the University of Applied Arts Vienna A cooperation of the department of Media Theory and the department of Philosophy. ‘Errant Intelligence’ challenges the prevailing biological and individualistic interpretations of machine learning, arguing instead for a radical understanding of machine intelligence. The book embraces the deviations, inconsistencies, and ‘errant behaviour’ as fundamental to the discovery of new knowledge, moving beyond the illusion of mere optimisation. Drawing on media theory, cybernetics, and a unique psychoanalytic lens, it explores the ‘technological unconscious’ of machine learning. It traces the historical roots of AI, from early automatons and the Turing machine to natural language processing and contemporary machine learning systems. Challenging the idea of an autonomous, self-generating AI, the book exposes the hidden labour, assumed logics, and inherent biases that animate its operation. It re-evaluates computational thinking, insisting on its inherently social, collective, and symbolic character, and revealing how language and logical paradoxes are not obstacles but constitutive forces that shape intelligent machines

candidateAudit.text: Zum Geburtstag von Udo Jürgens erinnern wir uns an einen ganz besonderen Gast Im Schweizerhaus haben sich immer schon die Prominenten gerne unter das Volk gemischt, so auch der unvergessliche Udo Jürgens. Er wäre am 30. September 92 Jahre alt geworden. Unvergessen bleibt er nicht nur als einer der größten deutschsprachigen Musiker, sondern auch als jemand, der die besondere Wiener Lebensart zu schätzen wusste. Auch bei uns im Schweizerhaus war Udo Jürgens gerne zu Gast. Hier konnte er auch als großer Star ganz selbstverständlich mitten unter den Gästen sitzen, ohne großes Aufsehen, bei einem frisch gezapften Budweiser Budvar und einer knusprigen Stelze. Denn genau das macht das Schweizerhaus schon immer aus: Bei uns treffen sich Menschen aus allen Lebensbereichen, Stammgäste, Prominente, Wiener Originale und Besucher aus aller Welt. Udo Jürgens hat diese ungezwungene Atmosphäre offenbar besonders geschätzt. Alles Gute zum Geburtstag und danke für die schönen Erinnerungen, die auch im Schweizerhaus Jubiläumsbuch von Herbert Lackner festgehalten wurden. Das Buch gibt es übrigens bei uns im Schweizerhaus in der Gästeinformation zum Preis von € 19,90.

candidateAudit.text: In this workshop with Helena Detsch we will explore simple ways to create a fascinating natural color palette from soil and plant-based materials like earths, minerals, vegetables, kitchen supplies and algae pigments. Part of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ Duration: 15:30–17:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio (free entry) Together, we'll first experiment with making self-made oil- or watercolors from 100% natural sources and then explore the many possibilities of sustainable painting, discovering how these self-made colors behave on paper and fabric and what a truly organic painting practice can look like. In her oil paintings, installations and animations, Helena Detsch explores (mis-)relationships between humans and more-than-human life. Her series and immersive spatial installations question Western anthropocentric narratives about nature as a resource and create spaces to reflect on coexistence and complex interconnections between human and other agents. To develop a more sustainable art practice, she crafts natural colors from plant and soil pigments. helena.kettu AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna dieangewandte

candidateAudit.title: About the next exhibition at AIL: Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and sever
candidateAudit.text: About the next exhibition at AIL: Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. What is happening beneath our feet? At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. With contributions by: Franziska Allerberger (Geographer), Michael Bahn (Ecologist), Helena Detsch (Visual Artist), Cornelia Dirnberger (Visual Artist), Christian Prohammer (Musician, Audio Engineer), Nora Schöpfer (Visual Artist), Konstantina Maria Serjannis (Cultural Scientist), Johanna Unterpertinger (Musician) ’03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). Join the extended exhibition program: 6 Oct Exhibition Opening with Performances by Michael Bahn, Johanna Unterpertinger and Christian Prohammer 8 Oct 15:30–17:30 Workshop with Helena Detsch The Organic Painter – Painting

candidateAudit.text: Während die Temperaturen langsam sinken, steigt die Lust auf gemütliche Backmomente zuhause. ✨ Ein herbstlich belegter Flammkuchen ist nicht nur einfach gemacht, sondern auch ein richtiges Wohlfühlrezept für die ganze Familie. 🎃🍂 Und das Beste daran? Jede:r kann den Teig nach Lust und Laune belegen ☺️ 👩🏼‍🍳Du brauchst: 300 g Mehl 1/2 TL Salz 150 ml Wasser 4 EL MANI Bläuel „Der Familienheld“ natives Olivenöl extra 100 g Crème Fraîche Salz und Pfeffer Abrieb von 1/2 Bio-Zitrone 250 g Hokkaido Kürbis 1 kleine rote Zwiebel 80 g MANI Bläuel Bio-Feta g.U.* 3 EL MANI Bläuel Kalamata Oliven in Scheiben 1 Zweig Thymian eine Handvoll Walnüsse *erhältlich im gut sortierten Bio-Fachhandel 👩🏼‍🍳Und so geht’s: 1. Mehl, Wasser, 3 EL Olivenöl und Salz zu einem geschmeidigen Teig verkneten, in eine geölte Schüssel geben und abgedeckt mindestens 30 Minuten bei Raumtemperatur ruhen lassen. 2. Den Backofen auf 190°C Heißluft vorheizen. 3. Crème Fraîche mit Salz, Pfeffer und Zitronenabrieb verrühren. 4. Kürbis in sehr dünne Scheiben und Zwiebel in feine Ringe schneiden und in einer Schüssel mit 1 EL Olivenöl vermengen. 5. Den Teig auf einem Backpapier sehr dünn ausrollen, mit der Creme bestreichen und mit Kürbisscheiben, Zwiebel, zerbröseltem Feta und Oliven belegen. 6. Bei 190°C Heißluft ca. 25-30 Minuten goldbraun und knusprig backen. Nach etwa 20 Minuten Backzeit die Walnüsse und den Thymian auf den Flammkuchen geben. 7. Den fertigen Flammkuchen nach Belieben mit etwas Olivenöl verfeinern. #maniolivenöl #herbstrezepte #flammkuchen #backenmitolivenöl

candidateAudit.text: We keep on digging and the next artistic research exhibition will open in October – Save the date and join us! Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. ’03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. candidateAudit.text: Some masterpieces are painted. Others are fired, glazed, and perfected by hand. For more than three centuries, Augarten Porcelain has embodied the elegance and craftsmanship of Vienna. The Masters of Vienna's Porcelain invites you beyond the showroom and into the heart of this extraordinary tradition, where master artisans continue to shape every piece with remarkable precision. Witness centuries of expertise come to life. Create your own porcelain keepsake under the guidance of those who have dedicated their lives to the craft. Then conclude your journey with an elegant afternoon tea, served on the very porcelain that has graced royal tables and distinguished homes for generations. This is more than a workshop. More than afternoon tea. It is an immersion into one of Vienna's most enduring expressions of artistry, where every detail is shaped by time, tradition, and exceptional craftsmanship. #rcmemories #TheRitzCarltonVienna #vienna #augarten

candidateAudit.title: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Appli
candidateAudit.text: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Applied Photography and Time-Based Media at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, which explores the synergistic potential of student teams from different degree programs. In collaboration with the department Industrial Design, this year’s focus was on the intersection of photography and the object, with particular attention paid to the relationship with set design, styling, casting and narrative. Seen from the perspective of Applied Photography, the object and thus the chair, is a welcome protagonist. Photography’s multiple applied genres are cited here: documentary, fashion, advertising, architecture and the portrait. When the function in Industrial Design coalesces with the idea of the purpose in Applied Photography, the question of factuality emerges. Be not mistaken: The most literal things are often the most confusing and enigmatic. Between what it is and how it is*, worlds unfold. We put the images to work. VDW Cocktail: 29 Sep, 17:00–18:00 Showcase and drinks followed by a collective walk to the billboards in front of the main entrance of the University Open Saturdays: 26 Sep / 3 Oct, 11:00–18:00 Opening hours: Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna The collaborative works are on display at the AIL and on the billboards at the university’s main entrance on Oskar-Kokoschka-Platz. dieangewandte viennadesignweek applied.photography angewandte_id Feat

candidateAudit.text: Ob pur, mariniert, kalt, warm, als Topping oder zum cremigen Dip püriert – Feta lässt sich vielseitig genießen und kann weitaus mehr als Salate verfeinern. ✨ Auch gebacken zeigt er, was in ihm steckt: Zusammen mit Kürbis, Zwiebel und Kräutern aus dem Ofen entsteht das perfekte Wohlfühlgericht für gemütliche Herbsttage. 🍂🎃 ✨Du brauchst: 600 g Hokkaido Kürbis 1 kleine rote Zwiebel 3 Rosmarinzweige 3 EL MANI Bläuel „Der Familienheld“ natives Olivenöl extra 1 Pkg. MANI Bläuel Bio-Feta g.U.* Salz und Pfeffer 1-2 EL MANI Bläuel Mediterraner Mix 1 Handvoll geröstete Cashews, grob gehackt *erhältlich im gut sortierten Bio-Fachhandel 👩🏼‍🍳Und so geht‘s: 1. Den Backofen auf 180°C O/U vorheizen. 2. Kürbis in ca. 1,5 cm große Würfel und die Zwiebel in Spalten schneiden. 3. Kürbis und Zwiebel in eine Auflaufform geben, mit etwas Salz, Pfeffer und 2 EL Olivenöl vermengen und 20 Minuten backen. 4. Die Form aus dem Ofen nehmen, den Rosmarin hinzufügen und alles kurz durchmischen. 5. Den Feta mittig zwischen das Gemüse setzen und mit 1 EL Olivenöl beträufeln. 6. Weitere 30-35 Minuten backen, bis der Kürbis und Feta weich sind. 7. Mit mediterranem Mix und gerösteten Cashews toppen und warm genießen. #ofenfeta #ofenkürbis #kürbisrezepte #biofeta #manibläuel

candidateAudit.text: 🔪 How well do you really know your 80s horror movies? 👻 Rodeho’s Rootin’ Tootin’ Pub Quiz returns to Villa Vida Café — and this time, we’re diving into the gloriously bloody, campy and unforgettable world of 1980s horror. 🩸📼 From slashers and supernatural nightmares to cult classics, monsters and final girls, it’s time to find out whether all those hours spent watching horror movies were actually educational. Hosted by drag artist Rodeho, expect horror trivia, drag, queer community and plenty of questionable knowledge finally getting its moment to shine. 📅 Friday, 23 October 2026 ⏰ 19:30–21:30 📍 Villa Vida Café Linke Wienzeile 102, 1060 Vienna 🎟 Donation-based 📝 Registration required — reserve your spot via the link in our bio. candidateAudit.text: 💘 Friends? Dates? Flirting? Something in between? Meet queer people in Vienna without swiping. 📅 Sat, 26 September 2026 ⏰ 19:00–21:00 📍 Villa Vida Café, Linke Wienzeile 102, 1060 Vienna 🎟️ €20 per person · cash at the door 💛 Soli tickets available 📝 Registration required 🌈 Who is it for? Queer people who want to meet other queer people — whether you’re looking for dating, friendship, flirting, new connections, or simply meeting more of the community. You’ll meet multiple people through a series of short mini-dates. Privately note who you’d like to connect with again — romantically, platonically, or otherwise. The structured format is there to make meeting people easier, including if you’re shy, introverted, or not into approaching strangers at a bar. 💛 Can’t comfortably afford €20? Soli tickets are available. Request one in the comments when registering — no explanation or justification needed. 🤝 Consent, boundaries and mutual respect are essential. A conversation or flirtation never creates an obligation to share contact details or meet again. Discriminatory or harassing behaviour is not welcome. ♿ Step-free access · accessible seating & toilet · service animals welcome. Please note that simultaneous conversations can mean significant background noise. 📝 Register via the link in bio/event page. Come as you are and see who you click with. 💘

candidateAudit.text: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is delighted to once again host one event in the program. unsafeandsounds AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna (Free entry) Overview: 18:30 Panel Discussion, unsafe+sounds in cooperation with the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures (University of Applied Arts Vienna) weibel.institute Affective Histories Timotheus Vermeulen and Christian Höller in conversation with Sophie Publig History is never simply given. It is made through the scales and materials by which the past becomes legible: from sweeping narratives and historical events to gestures, sounds, images, technical infrastructures, and seemingly minor traces SOPHIE PUBLIG is a Senior Scientist researching digital ecosystems. Based at the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, she navigates the intricate networks of online territories. TIMOTHEUS VERMEULEN is Professor of Media, Culture and Society at the University of Oslo and joint director of the Media Aesthetics Research Group. He was a visiting scholar in Art History at Harvard in 2023–24 and will serve as joint Principal Investigator on a project on the politics of tone at the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo in 2027–28. CHRISTIAN HÖLLER is editor and co-publisher of springerin – Hefte für Gegenwartskunst. candidateAudit.text: Gebackene Aubergine mit würziger Tomatensauce und zitronigem Kräuterjoghurt 🌿🍅 Ein Wohlfühlgericht aus der mediterranen Küche, das zwar zu jeder Jahreszeit begeistert, sich aber gerade jetzt anbietet, wo Auberginen in Saison sind ✨☺️ Unsere sonnengetrocknete Tomatenpaste ersetzt hier klassisches Tomatenmark und verleiht dem Gericht eine ganz besondere Tiefe und extra Würze 🍅 🌿Zutaten Für die Auberginen: 2 Auberginen (ca. 900g) 2 TL Salz 2-3 EL MANI Bläuel natives Olivenöl extra, Selection Für die Tomatensauce: 1 EL MANI Bläuel natives Olivenöl extra, Selection 2 Zehen MANI Bläuel Knoblauch in Olivenöl, fein gehackt 1/2 TL Kreuzkümmelsamen 1 TL gemahlener Koriander 1/2 TL Kardamom 1 Dose gehackte Tomaten 4 TL MANI Bläuel Tomatenpaste 1 TL Honig oder brauner Zucker Salz Für das Kräuterjoghurt: 250 g griechisches Joghurt 1 TL Zitronenabrieb 2 TL Minze, gehackt 2 TL Petersilie, gehackt etwas Salz Topping: frische Kräuter und Olivenöl 👩🏼‍🍳Zubereitung: Den Backofen auf 180°C Ober-/ Unterhitze vorheizen. Auberginen in ca. 1 cm dicke Scheiben schneiden. Mit Salz bestreuen und 20 Minuten ziehen lassen. Danach kurz abspülen, trocken tupfen und mit Olivenöl bepinseln. Die Auberginen auf ein mit Backpapier belegtes Blech legen und 35-45 Minuten backen. Nach der Hälfte der Zeit einmal wenden. Während die Auberginen im Ofen sind, die Tomatensauce zubereiten: das Olivenöl in einer Pfanne erhitzen und den Knoblauch mit den Gewürzen etwa eine Minute darin anbraten. candidateAudit.title: Das ist purer Olivengenuss, der den Sommer noch einmal aufleben lässt! 🌞🫒 🌿Du brauchst: 2 Scheiben Sauerteigbrot 125 g Burrata 90 g MANI Bläuel grüne & Kalamata Oliven al natura
candidateAudit.text: Das ist purer Olivengenuss, der den Sommer noch einmal aufleben lässt! 🌞🫒 🌿Du brauchst: 2 Scheiben Sauerteigbrot 125 g Burrata 90 g MANI Bläuel grüne & Kalamata Oliven al naturale, ohne Stein 1/2 Zitrone 2 EL MANI Bläuel „Der Familienheld“ natives Olivenöl extra 1 kleine Knoblauchzehe 1 kleine Handvoll Basilikum, frisch 2 EL Mandeln, grob gehackt 1 kleine Prise Chiliflocken (optional) etwas Meersalzflocken 👩🏼‍🍳Und so geht‘s: 1. Mandeln grob hacken und in einer trockenen Pfanne bei mittlerer Hitze goldbraun rösten, dann beiseitestellen. 2. Oliven in eine flache Schüssel geben und grob zerdrücken. Sie sollten etwas flacher, aber nicht zu einer Paste werden. 3. 1 EL Olivenöl, den Saft 1/2 Zitrone, Chiliflocken und die Hälfte des Basilikums zu den Oliven geben und vermengen. 4. Sauerteigbrot knusprig toasten und noch warm mit der Knoblauchzehe einreiben. 5. Burrata auf den beiden Toasts verteilen. 6. Die Olivenmischung darauf verteilen. Geröstete Mandeln und restliches Basilikum darübergeben. Etwas Olivenöl über das Brot träufeln und nach Belieben mit Meersalz toppen. 7. Zum Schluss die Zitronenschale direkt über beide Toasts reiben. 🍋 #maniolivenöl #toastie #olivenliebe #mediterraneküche #schnellerezepte

On Friday, 4 September 2026, Leila Szabo takes over our Day DJ session with a set centred on hyperpop with some dubstep. Expect an energetic mix of electronic sounds, sharp contrasts, heavy bass, and the genre-bending spirit of hyperpop. Whether you want to listen closely, catch up with friends, work with some decidedly non-background background music, or simply see where the set goes, you are welcome to join us. Date: Friday, 4 September 2026 Time: 16:00–18:00 Location: Villa Vida Café, Linke Wienzeile 102, 1060 Vienna DJ: Leila Szabo Music: Hyperpop, with some dubstep Entry: Free Meet the DJ: Leila Szabo For this edition of Day DJ, Leila Szabo brings hyperpop to Villa Vida Café. Hyperpop is known for pushing pop and electronic music beyond their usual boundaries. It can be bright, distorted, playful, chaotic, melodic, bass-heavy, or all of those things within the same track. What Is Day DJ at Villa Vida? Day DJ at Villa Vida Café is a regular series that gives local DJs space to share their sound in a daytime setting. The series focuses on new talent, experimentation, and community. Rather than putting DJs exclusively into a late-night club environment, Day DJ creates an accessible daytime space where artists can build sets, explore ideas, and connect with an audience. At the same time, the format is deliberately relaxed. You can come specifically for the music, meet friends for a drink, work from the café, or stay for the entire set. candidateAudit.text: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developing the project's multisensory scenography – the so-called SΫS SPACE. Aim of the Summer Studio is to prepare the prototype of the scenography, which will be established at the AIL in June 2027 as the centerpiece of the final exhibition of the PEEK project ’SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS — Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness.’ The SΫS SPACE facilitates a physical experience of one's own embededdness within living systems, within complex interrelationships – within a greater whole. It paves the way for relational sensing and thinking – an embodied systems awareness, that can help in coping with complexity, challenges, and uncertainties, and in making good decisions towards sustainable futures. It deliberately reduces the dominance of the sense of sight, placing the emphasis instead on smell, touch, and hearing. Numerous scientists, as well as invited artists, politicians, journalists, children, senior citizens, curators, cultural workers, educators, and teenagers are individually guided through the immersive environment by Jeanette Müller and Paul Divjak and share their responses in photo-based reflections and semi-structured interviews. Their feedback directly informs the prototype. Save the date! 14 and 15 Sep 2026 The SΫS SPACE will open to the public in individual time slots for an exclusive multisensory experience. candidateAudit.text: Day 2 of Liebe Isst Wurst 🤍 Hot, wholesome, slightly chaotic. We all managed to survive a heatwave through a combination of music, collective care, granita, water mist, electrolytes and vibes. Even a brief Stromausfall couldn’t stop us. Yesterday was joyful, sweaty, playful, a little chaotic, and full of genuine care and love. A huge thank you to our artists, our audience, our Awareness Team, and the incredible Würstelstand crew who kept everything running smoothly through one of the hottest weekdays of the year. Liebe Isst Wurst is about more than the lineup. It’s about creating a space where people can come together, feel welcome and safe, and love as bell hooks so eloquently describes. Participating in shaping Alltagskultur. One more day to go -> Come as you are. Come hydrated. See you at the Würstelstand. 🤍 #LiebeIsstWurst #wienerwürstelstand #queervienna #spittelau1090

candidateAudit.text: The pond is in Lower Austria. The garlic grows wild near Vienna.
